title: Nick Cannon hospitalized amid lupus battle, asks fans to 'pray for me'

 Anthony Robledo USA TODAY Nov. 20, 2026, 5:32 p.m. ET Hear this story Nick Cannon is asking for prayers amid a recent health scare.
 The comedian and actor, 46, confirmed he was hospitalized in a Friday, Nov. 20, Instagram post after battling lupus, an autoimmune disease that damages organs and tissue.
 The "Raising the Cannons" star shared a photo of himself lying in a hospital bed wearing a face mask and head piece. He attached Donny Hathaway's 1971 track "A Song for You" to the post.
 "This 🌎can definitely take a lot out of you!" he wrote in text featured in the photo. "Pray for me y'all."
 While Cannon did not elaborate on his condition, he captioned the post "#LupusWarrior."

 USA TODAY has reached out to Cannon's representatives for comment.
 Cannon is a father of 12 children with six different women. His youngest is Halo Marie Cannon, 3, whom he shares with model Alyssa Scott. In 2021, they welcomed Zen Cannon , who died at five months old after battling brain cancer.
 What is lupus?
 According to the Cleveland Clinic , lupus is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks healthy tissues and organs throughout the body.
 The disease causes inflammation that can affect the skin, joints, blood and organs, including the kidneys, lungs and heart, per the Cleveland Clinic.
 The Mayo Clinic states that diagnosing lupus is difficult as symptoms vary from person to person and can change over time.
 There are multiple forms of lupus, including the most common, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), which affects more than 200,000 people in the United States, according to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention .
